judged_text: The duplicate check compares emails case-sensitively (`guest === attendee.email`) while the blacklist is lowercased only on the environment-variable side, so case variation defeats both guards. Submitting 'Guest@Example.com' when 'guest@example.com' already attends inserts a second attendee row for the same person — duplicate emails and duplicate ICS attendee entries — and 'Banned@Example.com' bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS because the submitted guest is never lowercased before the includes check.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the duplicate/blacklist filtering uses raw `guest` strings without normalization: `guest === attendee.email` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. The blacklist values are explicitly lowercased (`map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but `guest` is not, so case variants can bypass the blacklist. Likewise, the duplicate check is case-sensitive and can allow inserting a second attendee differing only by email case via `attendees.createMany`, leading to duplicate attendee rows and downstream duplicate ICS/email attendee entries.
